wrong: Found by the first Codex audit before any job: the integer Fourier frequencies were in the optimised parameter tree, so Adam would have moved them and broken periodicity without any divergence check noticing. Fixed (gradient zeroed, frequencies asserted at every save/load) before the pilot.

The bank-training plan changed twice. As first registered (DESIGN §3), one 5-hour fit per bank at R = 64 (two architectures), 128 and 256. After the pilot, A3 replaced it with 10-hour fits of architecture A at R = 64/128/256 with a band-limit penalty. Those fits were cancelled when the user froze the pilot bank (A4). Bar (a) as registered fails and was relaxed to 'accepted at about 1 %'; bar (b) was replaced by a bar relative to the bank's own floor. The 'R needed to match POD-64' question is unanswered.

The frozen bank was fitted without the band-limit penalty that the pilot's diagnostics argued for: the network has detail finer than a 32³ grid resolves, so the 32³ reading of the bank is a measurably different bank from the 64³/96³ readings (pre-Löwdin deviation and cross-mesh tables). This is the most likely reason the 32³ floor differs from the other two, but it is an inference: no band-limited bank was evaluated, and these diagnostics do not isolate the cause.

The autodiff vs FFT derivative disagreement first read as a correctness problem. It shrinks when the same network is read finer, which points to under-resolution of the network on the grid; the frame never uses the autodiff derivative but the exact spectral derivative of the bank actually used, checked in every job. Nothing was retracted; the in-job autodiff comparison on the tests stays a flag at 32³.
answer: **Mechanically, yes.** One frozen network file, read at 32³, 64³ and 96³ with no per-mesh fitting of the bank, runs the co-moving reduced model at every mesh: the frame solves its shift, the frame-frozen control fails as it must, and on both cohorts the head's evolved worst is close to its bank's floor at every mesh (worst / floor columns above). At 96³ the head is faster than its CNAB2 comparator by more than the speed bar on both cohorts.

**As a replacement for the per-mesh POD bank at the POD's accuracy, no.** Accuracy is set by the bank, and this frozen fit's floor is many times the POD-64 floor at every mesh. Its training loss is far above the optimum of its own objective (the same-data POD), so the gap is between this fit and what the objective allows; whether longer optimisation, more capacity or a different sampling would close it was not tested. Judged by the pre-registered bars (a) and (b), the result fails; the bars used for the verdict were relaxed by the user after the pilot (A4).

**Bar (c), the main question, fails as pre-registered.** At 64³ and 96³ the head error and the floor agree closely; the 32³ reading has a lower floor, a pre-Löwdin deviation an order of magnitude larger, and columns that differ strongly from the finer readings after restriction. The head's max/min ratio passes on development; the floor's ratio misses narrowly; the orthonormality sub-criterion fails at every mesh, including 64³ and 96³. The supported statement is therefore limited: on the two finer meshes tested, one coordinate-network bank gave nearly mesh-independent errors; on the coarsest mesh it read as a measurably different bank, most likely because the network carries detail that grid cannot resolve. Whether a band-limited fit removes that discrepancy is open.
open: A bank fitted with the band-limit penalty (A3) is the direct test of whether the 32³ discrepancy comes from this artifact's under-resolved detail; the cancelled fits would have tested it.
The floor gap to POD-64: longer fits and larger ranks were started (A3) but cancelled and never evaluated.
The heads are trained per mesh; a single head shared across meshes was not tested.
